data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise common conjunctions that connect events in time and explain reasons.
learningPoints: Use when to link events around the same time.
Use before and after to show order.
Use while for an action happening during another action.
Use because to give a reason.
Use so to give a result.
Choose the conjunction that accurately expresses the relationship between clauses.

sections.explain: WHEN links one event to the time of another event.

words.word: Call me when you get home.
Call me because you get home.
Call me so you get home.

sections.explain: BEFORE shows that one action happens earlier than another.

words.word: Wash your hands before you eat.
Wash your hands after you eat first.
Wash your hands because you eat.

sections.explain: AFTER shows that one action happens later than another.

words.word: We went for a walk after we finished lunch.
We went for a walk because we finished lunch.
We went for a walk before we finished lunch.

sections.explain: WHILE links actions happening at the same time, especially longer actions.

words.word: I listened to music while I was cooking.
I listened to music because I was cooking.
I listened to music after I was cooking at the same time.

sections.explain: BECAUSE introduces the reason for an action or situation.

words.word: I stayed home because I was ill.
I stayed home so I was ill.
I stayed home when I was ill because.

sections.explain: SO introduces a result or consequence.

words.word: It was cold, so I closed the window.
It was cold because I closed the window.
It was cold before I closed the window because.

sections.explain: WHEN can introduce a shorter event in a past situation.

words.word: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
I was sleeping because the phone rang.
I was sleeping so the phone rang.

sections.explain: BEFORE can link two actions without using WILL in the time clause.

words.word: Check the door before you leave.
Check the door because you leave.
Check the door so you leave.

sections.explain: BECAUSE gives the cause; SO gives the result.

words.word: The bus was late, so I missed the start.
The bus was late because I missed the start.
The bus was late while I missed the start.

sections.explain: AFTER clearly shows that the second action follows the first.

words.word: After I finished work, I went home.
Because I finished work, I went home after.
While I finished work, I went home before.
